The Supreme Court press note of 21 July 2026 states that messages on the public Telegram channel @Alviseperez, from at least October 2024 to December 2025, named the mayor of Algeciras and urged him to resign, warning that otherwise content on allegedly criminal conduct would be published; the instructor cites article 172.1 (coacciones) or alternatively 169.1 (amenazas condicionales) of the Penal Code.

The 21 July 2026 suplicatorio was the fourth sent by the Supreme Court; two earlier ones (illegal party financing and electoral offence over 100,000 euros in cash from a cryptocurrency businessman; messages about the Valencia hate-crimes prosecutor) had already been granted.

On 1 July 2026 the Supreme Court's Sala de lo Penal opened a case for possible provocation of aggravated public disorder (art. 557.4 Penal Code) over messages on 'Canal Alvise' calling for occupying and blocking roads, logistics centres, ports and refineries; a Comisaría General de Información report on the channel's ownership and control was cited, and Carmen Lamela was appointed instructor.
In May 2025 the Supreme Court had declined the same case for lack of evidence linking him to the channel and returned it to a Madrid investigating court.

On 19 May 2026 the European Parliament plenary lifted his immunity so the Supreme Court could investigate alleged illegal financing of SALF's 2024 European campaign; the Legal Affairs Committee had backed it by 20 votes to 0 with one abstention.

The Supreme Court investigates whether he received 100,000 euros in cash from crypto businessman Álvaro Romillo ('CryptoSpain') before the 2024 European campaign; he admitted before the court in July 2025 that he received it and says it was for personal use, while prosecutors say it was for the campaign and was not declared to the Tribunal de Cuentas.
In February 2024 he posted messages and photos of Valencia prosecutor Susana Gisbert on his Telegram channel; the first suplicatorio against him concerned this.

On 3 September 2025 posted a 'Se busca' notice with a photo of a young man he described as leader of a group of 'menas' in Torrevieja, asking followers for information to locate him; the channel then had over 654,000 subscribers.

Analysis of 195 messages posted between 10 May and 9 June 2024 found a mean of 271,070.77 views and 12,792.89 reactions per message; daily posting averaged 4.67, 4.5, 9.57 and 6.9 messages across four campaign phases.

According to Marcelino Madrigal's analysis for Newtral, the original messages he published later accounted for 66% of the views (more than 40 million unique views) of all analysed Telegram messages on electoral fraud in Spain, with no other channel reaching 8%; his messages reached maximum weight at the 2024 European elections.

Newtral's analysis states that in 2026 most messages spreading electoral-fraud narratives no longer originate from his channel but from channels such as 'une80', 'HazteOirorg', 'rafapalreal' and 'NosObservan'.
Attended the 2 August 2026 protest at the Moroccan embassy in Madrid and unfurled a banner reading 'Not a meter, not a euro to Morocco'.

In September 2025 the discussion chat linked to the channel had over 92,000 members (100,397 according to a Supreme Court statement); its disclaimer states the channel's owner is not Pérez and asks for donations.

After the 3 September 2025 'Se busca' post, users in the chat posted calls for 'grupos de caza' and messages such as 'guillotina o a Marruecos' and 'mejor decapitar'; the administrator 'Ardilla Pérez' did not delete them.
SALF won nearly 800,000 votes and three seats in the 2024 European elections; in the 2026 Andalusian elections it won over 105,000 votes (2.5%) and no seats.
Investigators say Álvaro Romillo promoted crypto wallets for donations to the party.

Vox pushed 'prioridad nacional' in regions it governs with the PP and, after a July 2026 Issep summer course where Jorge Buxadé and Hermann Tertsch spoke, sought to place 'remigración' in the national debate, defined as repatriation of illegal entrants, deportation of legal entrants who commit crimes, and remigration of those dependent on subsidies or not integrating.

On 6 October 2026 Vox Congress spokesperson Pepa Rodríguez de Millán asked voters to vote in person, as Abascal had done the day before, cited alleged postal-vote-buying cases in Albaida del Aljarafe (Sevilla) and Melilla, and asked the JEC to apply the Supreme Court order suspending the external vote of 'ley de nietos' nationals.

At Vox's request, Section Four of the Supreme Court's Contencioso-Administrativo Chamber provisionally suspended voting rights for more than 160,000 CERA registrants, citing a 'peligro fundado, real y serio' of altering election results; the JEC had said nationality questions exceed its competence.
On 16 July 2026 the JEC rejected a precautionary suspension of CERA registrations requested by Vox and others, stating the electoral administration 'no puede sustituir el criterio del legislador'.

The Objective reported on 28 November 2025 that the anonymous X account @eljudiodevox, which attacked former Vox leaders and Alvise Pérez, was run by Vox affiliate Fran Bouzas; Bouzas denied it and a source said Vox had asked affiliates for a 'unidad estratégica digital'.

On 29 March 2026 Alvise Pérez announced he would seek prison for Fran Bouzas, identified as administrator of 'El Judío de Vox', for not clarifying whether Vox communications coordinator Álvaro Zancajo ordered the attacks; the article presents this as Pérez's claim.

A 2019 ISD investigation cited by First Draft found a Venezuela-origin network of nearly 3,000 Twitter accounts supporting Vox, averaging 152,907 tweets a day in 2019 and mentioning Santiago Abascal about 460,000 times.

On 1 July 2026 a Madrid investigating court issued a detention order against Vito Quiles after he ignored two summonses in a case over a claim that a Hacienda official was an adviser to María Jesús Montero; he had published the man's full name and photo.

As of July 2026 he had four active proceedings (hate crime at a 2024 protest, revelation of secrets over Beatriz Corredor's address, slander against Facua's Rubén Sánchez, and the Madrid hoax case) and two archived complaints (Begoña Gómez, Sara Santaolalla).

In September 2026 Vaquero travelled to Ceuta with party militants and posted a video from the border saying 'España debe defender su frontera y debe deportar a los inmigrantes ilegales'; the party described the July entries as an 'invasión'.

Revuelta's president Jaime Hernández was formerly spokesperson of Hazte Oír and right-hand man to its president Ignacio Arsuaga; businessman Marcial Cuquerella, who has admitted membership of El Yunque, backed Hernández.
